0.0.n: An English greeting borrowed into Japanese, used casually to open the video.

0.1.n: The platform name is used to address the audience here.

0.3.n: Part of ということで, a common phrase for moving into the main topic.

0.4.n: This noun helps form ということで; it does not refer to a physical thing.

0.5.n: Completes ということで, which introduces what the speaker will discuss next.

0.7.n: Sets the time for the recording.

0.8.n: Marks 今日 as the topic rather than the person doing the recording.

0.9.n: Here です adds politeness during a pause, rather than completing a statement.

0.10.n: Softens the introduction and keeps the listener engaged.

0.12.n: With で, describes the recording as prompted by something urgent.

0.13.n: Links 緊急 to the recording action, describing its circumstances.

0.14.n: Names what the speaker is recording.

0.15.n: Marks 動画 as the thing affected by 回す.

0.16.n: 回す becomes 回して + おります, a humble, polite ongoing form; here 回す means to run the camera.

1.0.n: Sets the time frame as the speaker starts introducing the topic.

1.1.n: Used with ね as a conversational filler after 今日.

1.2.n: Keeps the listener engaged while the speaker pauses.

1.4.n: The name of a programming language, introduced as the video's topic.

1.5.n: Introduces a name; the description of what bears that name follows after a pause.

1.6.n: Inserted with ね while the speaker plans the next part of the sentence.

1.7.n: Softens the pause rather than asking for an answer.

2.0.n: A technical term for processing on a server rather than in the user's browser.

2.2.n: A borrowed English noun; Japanese does not explicitly mark it as singular or plural here.

2.3.n: Marks ウェブサイト as what can be built.

2.5.n: A shortened まあ, used as a casual filler while explaining.

2.7.n: Combines with に to describe how websites can be built.

2.8.n: Turns 簡単 into a description of the building action.

2.9.n: A noun for construction; with できる, it expresses the ability to build.

2.10.n: After 構築, expresses that building is possible; this is the plain form.

3.0.n: Points back to building websites, the purpose just described.

3.1.n: Refers to what the language is used for, not a cause.

3.2.n: Links そのため to 言語, describing a language intended for that purpose.

3.3.n: In this computing context, 言語 refers to a programming language rather than a spoken language.

3.4.n: Adds a polite ending to the description of PHP as a language.

3.5.n: Softens the explanation and invites the listener to follow along.

3.7.n: The programming language's name is repeated as the speaker resumes the introduction.

3.8.n: A conversational version of という, used to introduce a name.

3.9.n: Stands in for a noun: PHPっていうの means something called PHP.

3.10.n: Marks the language called PHP as the thing that exists.

3.11.n: Used for things rather than people; here it introduces the existence of this language.

3.12.n: Short for の in んです, presenting the statement as background for what comes next.

3.13.n: Makes the explanation polite as part of んです.

3.14.n: A soft connector that leaves room for the next point, not necessarily a strong contrast.

0.lit: Hello, YouTube! So, today, you see, on an urgent basis, I am recording a video.
0.tip: 動画を回す means to record a video, not literally to spin one.

1.lit: Today, you see, called PHP, you see…
1.tip: The repeated ですね phrases are polite pauses; PHPという introduces a name whose description continues in the following lines.

2.lit: Server-side, websites, well, easily can build…
2.tip: 構築できる means can build; できる expresses ability without needing する.

3.lit: A language for that purpose, you see; there is one called PHP, but…
3.tip: PHPっていうのがある introduces something called PHP, using casual っていう instead of という.
